slot.brief: Wire stretched to a given multiple of original length (volume constant); find ratio of new to original resistance, then compare power dissipated at same voltage across both.

stem: A wire of resistance $2\ \Omega$ is stretched to three times its original length, keeping its volume constant. It is then connected across a $6$ V battery. The power dissipated in the wire is:
working: Volume constant: $A' \ell' = A \ell$, with $\ell' = 3\ell$, so $A' = A/3$. New resistance $R' = \dfrac{\rho \ell'}{A'} = \dfrac{\rho (3\ell)}{A/3} = 9\,\dfrac{\rho \ell}{A} = 9R = 18\ \Omega$. Power $P = \dfrac{V^2}{R'} = \dfrac{6^2}{18} = \dfrac{36}{18} = 2\ \text{W}$.
solution:
With volume constant, $A'\ell'=A\ell$ and $\ell'=3\ell$, so $A'=A/3$. Thus, $R'=\rho\ell'/A'=9R=18\,\Omega$.
$$P=\frac{V^2}{R'}=\frac{6^2}{18}=2\,\text{W}$$
